confirm.needs_yes: stdin is not a terminal, so there is no way to confirm; add -yes to run anyway.
invite.need_addr: Give the address clients use to reach this node with -addr HOST:PORT (repeat for more). Addresses on this host that look public: {addrs}
invite.created_note: Send the line above to whoever will run checks against this node. It works like a password: don't post it anywhere public. To revoke: connverifier invite revoke -label {label}
invite.list_row: {label}  created {created}  sessions ≤{sessions}  connections ≤{connections}  new ≤{rate}/s  duration ≤{duration}  idle ≤{idle}
check.tcp-capacity.title: TCP long-lived connections
tcp_capacity.confirm.notice: About to open and hold {connections} TCP connections to node "{node}" ({addr}), at most {rate} new ones per second, for {duration_ms}. This fills connection tables in your router and your provider's NAT; other devices on the same network may briefly lose connectivity.
tcp_capacity.confirm.notice_until_stoppe: About to open and hold {connections} TCP connections to node "{node}" ({addr}), at most {rate} new ones per second, until you stop it or the node's session ends. This fills connection tables in your router and your provider's NAT; other devices on the same network may briefly lose connectivity.
param.duration_ms.zero: until interrupted or the node's session ends
metric.heartbeats.interval_acked: Heartbeats acknowledged after a full idle interval
tcp_capacity.error.no_connection: No connection could be made; failed dials: {dial_errors}. Last error: {last_error}
tcp_capacity.error.no_connection_host_re: No connection could be made; all {dial_errors} dials failed because this host ran out of file descriptors or ephemeral ports — the machine running the tool, not the network. Last error: {last_error}
tcp_capacity.warning.ended_before_connec: The run ended before any connection completed; there is no data to judge.
tcp_capacity.warning.host_resource: Dials that failed because this host ran out of file descriptors or ephemeral ports: {count}. The result shows this machine's limit, not the network's.
tcp_capacity.warning.fd_limit: This host's open-file limit is {limit}, too low for {target} connections; the result is bounded by the host, not the network. Raise ulimit -n, including the hard limit, or lower -clients.
tcp_capacity.warning.port_range: This host has {ports} ephemeral ports, which caps connections to one node address below the target of {target}; the result is bounded by the host, not the network.
tcp_capacity.inference.silent_drops: Connections that stopped answering without a close or reset: {count}. This is the usual sign of a NAT or other middlebox silently dropping connection state.
tcp_capacity.inference.peer_closed: Connections closed by the far side without a reason: {count}. The node always states a reason before it closes a connection, so this points to a middlebox sending the close, or the node process exiting abnormally.
tcp_capacity.inference.reset_or_error: Connections ended by a reset or another error: {count}.
tcp_capacity.inference.bad_ack: Connections whose heartbeat reply differed from what was sent: {count}. Something on the path rewrote data, or the far side is not an echo node.
tcp_capacity.not_proven.lifetime_upper_b: A silently dropped connection is only noticed when a heartbeat reply times out, so its lifetime is an upper bound, long by up to one heartbeat interval ({heartbeat_ms}); closed or reset connections are noticed at once.
tcp_capacity.not_proven.no_full_interval: No connection was seen idle for a full heartbeat interval ({heartbeat_ms}), so whether connections survive idleness was not tested.
metric.handshake_errors: Connected but did not finish the ticket handshake
metric.drops.node_closed: Drops (closed by the node, with a reason)
node.label: Name
node.observed_addr: This host's address as the node saw it
node.grant_value: connections {connections} · new per second {rate} · length {duration_ms} · idle {idle_ms}{stamp}
session.error.node_identity: The node at {addr} presented a key that does not match the invite, so the run stopped before sending the token. The invite may be stale (the node changed its key), the address wrong, or the connection intercepted.
session.error.node_unreachable: Could not reach the node's control port: {error}
session.error.node_busy: The node is full and opened no session ({reason}): {message}. Try again in {retry_after_ms}.
tcp_capacity.error.rejected_auth: The node rejected the ticket on all {count} connections: the session may have been ended or the invite revoked.
tcp_capacity.error.handshake_failed: The node was reachable, but none of {count} connections finished the ticket handshake; something on the path may interfere. Last error: {last_error}
tcp_capacity.warning.idle_too_short: The node granted an idle period of {idle_ms}, shorter than the {needed_ms} a heartbeat and its reply need: it would close every connection itself, so the run did not start. Lower -heartbeat or ask the node for a longer idle period.
tcp_capacity.warning.node_busy: Connections the node turned away because it was full: {count}. The result shows the node's limit, not the network's.
tcp_capacity.warning.node_quota: Connections the node turned away for quota: {count}. The result shows the invite's quota, not the network's.
tcp_capacity.warning.granted_less: The node granted {granted} connections, fewer than the {asked} asked for: the asked-for scale was not tested.
tcp_capacity.warning.dial_rate_cut: The node lowered new connections per second from {asked} to {granted}: the ramp-up is slower; drop judgements are unaffected.
tcp_capacity.warning.duration_cut: The run ended because the node's session was about to expire ({granted_ms}), not at -duration.
tcp_capacity.inference.node_closed: Connections the node closed and said why: {count} ({reasons}). These are not evidence of network drops.
tcp_capacity.not_proven.handshake_errors: Connections that connected but did not finish the ticket handshake: {count}. The path or the node misbehaved before admission; the client cannot tell which.
check.udp-baseline.title: UDP round trip and loss
check.tcp-baseline.title: TCP round trip
metric.late: Of those, replies that came late
metric.lost.forward: Lost on the way to the node
metric.loss.forward: Loss on the way to the node
metric.duplicates.forward: Duplicated on the way to the node
metric.reordered.forward: Reordered on the way to the node
metric.node_residence.p50: Time the node held a packet, p50
metric.node_residence.p99: Time the node held a packet, p99
metric.send_slip.over_10ms: Probes sent more than 10 ms late
metric.send_errors: Probes this host failed to send
baseline.warning.duration_not_granted: The node granted a session of {granted_ms}, shorter than the run needs, so the check did not run.
baseline.warning.rate_not_granted: The node allows {granted} STAMP packets per second, fewer than the {asked} the check sends, so the check did not run.
baseline.warning.send_slip: Probes this host sent more than 10 ms behind schedule: {count}. The machine could not keep up, so the samples no longer follow the stated schedule.
baseline.not_proven.host_load: This host's CPU load and other traffic during the run were not checked; either can add delay that is not the network's.
udp_baseline.unsupported.invite_without_: The invite names no UDP port; ask the node's operator for a new invite.
udp_baseline.unsupported.node_without_st: The node runs no STAMP reflector or does not allow this invite to use it.
udp_baseline.error.no_socket: Could not open a UDP socket to the node: {error}
udp_baseline.error.no_udp_to_node: No UDP packet reached the node. Something blocks UDP to it — on this path or at the node's firewall; the check cannot tell which.
udp_baseline.error.no_reply: No reply came back, and the node did not report what it received, so the direction of the loss is unknown.
udp_baseline.inference.return_blocked: The node received the probes but no reply came back: UDP from the node to this host appears to be blocked.
udp_baseline.warning.node_slow: Packets the node held more than 10 ms before answering: {count}. The node, not the network, added that delay.
udp_baseline.warning.over_rate: Packets the node dropped for exceeding the granted rate: {count}. They would look like network loss.
udp_baseline.warning.address_changed: Packets that reached the node from another source address of this host: {count}. A NAT changed the mapping during the run.
udp_baseline.inference.loss: Probes without a reply in time: {count}, of which replies that came late: {late}.
udp_baseline.inference.duplicates: Duplicated packets — on the way to the node: {forward}; on the way back: {return}.
udp_baseline.inference.reordering: Replies that arrived out of order: {count}; of them reordered on the way to the node: {forward}.
udp_baseline.not_proven.direction_unknow: The node did not report what it received, so loss is not split into the way there and the way back.
udp_baseline.not_proven.return_after_for: Return-path loss is measured only on packets that reached the node; with loss on the way there it rests on fewer samples.
udp_baseline.not_proven.send_errors: Probes this host could not send: {count}. They are left out of every count.
tcp_baseline.not_proven.node_scheduling: The node's own handling time is not separated from the round trip.
tcp_baseline.error.broke: The connection ended before any echo came back: {error}
tcp_baseline.inference.broke: The connection ended during the run: {error}. Samples up to then are kept.
tcp_baseline.inference.stalls: Echoes that did not come back within the waiting time: {count}. On TCP a lost segment shows up as such a delay: the stream waits for its retransmission.
tcp_baseline.warning.node_refused: The node refused the connection for its own limits ({reason}).
tcp_baseline.error.rejected: The node refused the session ticket ({reason}).
tcp_baseline.error.no_connection: Could not connect to the node: {error}
tcp_baseline.error.handshake_failed: The node did not answer the session ticket: {error}
baseline.warning.interrupted: The run was interrupted before this check measured anything.
